To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the subcellular location of NADPH-hydroxypyruvates (NADPH-hydroxypruvate reductase) in pea leaves is mainly in the supernatants (cytosolic fraction) and that a minor activity is found in the chloroplasts and peroxisomes.
the major site of NADPH-hydroxypyruvates reduction is the cytosol.

NADPH-dependent HPR activity was found to be predominantly located in the cytosolic fraction of pea leaf protoplasm, and that this enzyme could be involved in the oxidative carbon cycle of photorespiration, functioning as an auxiliary reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the NAD(P)H-dependent hydroxypyrruvate reductases and glyoxylate reducers in photorespiratory metabolism and the subcellular location of these activities.
elucidation of the subcellular location and function of the NAD(P)H-dependent reductases of photorespiratory metabolism.
the subcellular location of NADPH dependent hydroxypyruate reductase activity (NADPH HPR) in pea leaf protoplast lysate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NADPH-dependent HPR activity of leaf protoplasts is localized mainly in the cytosolic compartment.
the role of NADPHHPR in photorespiration remains unclear.
NADPH-dependent HPR and GR are not localized in peroxisomes and are not involved in the peroxysomal photorespiratory carbon oxidation cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NADPH-HPL is a cytosolic enzyme, which is not involved in photorespiration.
NADPH-HPL is not an essential component of the photorespiratory pathway.

the cytosolic localization of NADPH-Glyoxylate Reductase (NADPGR) in the leaf of Pisum sativa and the chloroplasts localization of NADPGR in the leaf of Spinacia oleracea are in agreement with the results of previous work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an NADPH-dependent HPR that is located in the cytosolic compartment of pea leaves.
there is a significant amount of NADPH dependent hydroxypyruate reductase in the cytosolic fraction of the leaf protoplasts.
NADPH-HRP activity is located predominantly in the supernatants of leaf protoplasts.
